citation.title: Latent Diffusion Models for Structural Component Design
citation.authors: Ethan Herron, Jaydeep Rade, Anushrut Jignasu, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian, Aditya Balu, Soumik Sarkar, and Adarsh Krishnamurthy

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across the evaluation set, generated designs have no substantial difference in predicted strain energy from SIMP-optimized designs; mean absolute volume-fraction error is also reported.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No ML-versus-classical speed or cost ratio reported.
claim.alternatives: Abstract: structural performance and variability are supported quantitatively; Section 6.4 reports training times across resolutions, not an ML-versus-classical timing comparison.

baseline.problem_size: 3D voxel grids: 32^3, 64^3, and 128^3; evaluation uses 100 SIMP designs and 2,000 generated designs (Sections 5, 6.1)
baseline.training_time: Section 6.4: VAE training about 2 min 20 s/epoch at 32^3 and about 24 min/epoch at 64^3; 128^3 multigrid training under 2 h; diffusion training about 6, 22, and 95 ms/sample for 32^3, 64^3, and 128^3
baseline.data_generation_cost: Section 5: 66,000 32^3 samples, 25,000 64^3, and 10,000 128^3; Section 6.2 says intermediate samples are saved over an average of 13 iterations per initial strain energy; total generation time not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Predicted strain energy; voxel-derived volume fraction
baseline.quality_gap: Section 6.2: generated versus SIMP design volume-fraction mean absolute error 0.0989; strain-energy distributions described as having no substantial aggregate difference.

R1.evidence: Section 6.2 compares predicted quality; no speed comparison to match on quality or time.

R2.evidence: Sections 5–6 report no classical-versus-ML speed comparison.

R3.evidence: No speed claim is made as the primary outcome; Section 6.4 gives model training times only.

R4.evidence: Section 6.2 says strain energy for generated designs is predicted by an evaluation neural network; returned designs are not reported as FE-verified, and failure rates are absent.

reporting.n_test_cases: 100 evaluation initial-strain-energy samples; 2,000 generated and 100 SIMP designs (Section 6.1)

notes: No public code availability statement was found in the coded text. Quality comparisons use surrogate-predicted strain energy rather than reported FE analyses of returned designs.
